To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have studied the structure of β-carotenes deposited on Cu (1,1,1), using scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and low temperature scanning tunneling microscopy at liquid nitrogen (LTSTM) temperature, we have observed the formation of self-organized molecular layers, and we have identified the molecules by their internal structure.

all-trans β-carotenes on a Cu (1 11) surface self-assemble into a periodic structure that is characterized by a 2D unit cell with the dimensions 2.2 nm × 1.1 nm and that the β-ionone end rings are oriented perpendicular to the Cu (1 11) plane.

β-carotene forms a self-organized molecular layer structure with an ordered molecular arrangement on Cu (1 1 1), that the STM image reveals the internal structure of the molecule and that the molecule is flexible enough to allow for a large three-dimensional extension.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the self-organization of all-trans β-carotenes on Cu (1,1,1) by scanning tunneling microscopy.
the study of the self-organized molecular layers of all-trans β-carotenes on Cu (1 1 1) at liquid nitrogen temperature by means of scanning tunneling microscopy.
the investigation of the structure of self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) of organic compounds on solid substrates, in particular on metal surfaces, using scanning tunneling microscopy (STM).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the β-carotene molecule is able to form a well ordered and stable structure on Cu (1,1,1) at room temperature.
the molecules are arranged on the surface in a way that allows them to form the largest possible three-dimensional structures.
β-carotene forms a well-organized self-assembled multilayer structure on Cu (1 1 1) at room temperature, which is stable up to 77 K.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the β-carotene molecule is able to form a well-ordered multilayered self-organized structure with a high degree of order and with a large number of molecules per layer.
the β-carotene layer is a self-organized, three-dimensional structure, which is stabilized by van der Waals interactions and which has a large periodic extension.
we have shown how a single molecular layer on a metal surface can self-organize in a three-dimensional structure, and that STM can resolve the molecular structure of the molecules in this structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to study the self-organization of molecules on a metal surface by STM.
the STM can provide a detailed view on the structure of large organic molecules and their self-organization on surfaces, which may be important for the development of new organic electronics devices.
the STM can be used to study the self-organization of organic molecules in the solid state.
